Michigan Senate candidate Abdul el Sayed cited Anthropic research warning of rogue AI to demand an industry pause, government ownership, and heavy stock taxes.

The Poison:
Weaponizing genuine safety research to justify sweeping government takeovers and punitive taxation of emerging technology.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing the tool for the governance. Using metaphysical existential dread (WHAT) to justify bureaucratic power grabs (WHO).

Social Physics Analysis:
El Sayed runs a classic Smart Selfish maneuver. He takes real industry safety concerns (pretext) and reframes them as an existential emergency to justify government ownership and punitive taxes, consolidating state power while masking bureaucratic extraction.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. Inverted policy pretexts generate bureaucratic stagnation.

The Unavoidable Truth: AI safety presents genuine systemic risks requiring careful governance.

The Unavoidable Lie: State ownership and punitive taxation are neutral solutions rather than power grabs.
